sentences.text: The petitioner has sought for quashing of the endorsement at Annexure-D, whereby the endorsement is issued to the effect that reference was made beyond the period of six weeks from the date of the Award and accordingly, there is no provision to accept and act upon such petition.
2. The facts are that the petitioner's lands have been acquired for the purpose of development of Highway.

The Award was passed and aggrieved by the amount fixed, the petitioner has made out the representation at Annexure-'B' seeking the matter to be referred to the Court of Senior Civil Judge,
Mandya in order to enable the fixation of price.
The petitioner has also annexed the petition under Section 35(2) of the Karnataka Highways Act, 1964 made before the Civil Court along with the said application.

The said application at Annexure-'B' has been rejected as per the endorsement at Annexure-'D' dated 25.05.2018 on NC: 2023:KHC:23788 the ground that reference application ought to have been made within six weeks of the date of Award.
The said endorsement is challenged before this Court.

3. A perusal of the endorsement at Annexure-D would make it clear that the endorsement has rejected the request for reference on the ground that the application ought to have been made after the period of six weeks from the date of passing of the Award.

Section 35(2) of the Karnataka Highways Act, 1964 reads as follows:-
"35. Reference against the award of Highway Authority or authorised officer under section 28.-
 (1) xxx  (2) Any such application shall be made within six weeks from the date of the award, and shall be in such form as may be prescribed."
4. In the present case, it is not in dispute that the Award has been passed on 28.12.2017.
The representation of the petitioner at Annexure-'B' seeking NC: 2023:KHC:23788 for reference is made on 12.02.2018.
The petitioner along with the said representation has annexed the copy of the petition filed before the court under Section 35 (2) of the Karnataka Highways Act, 1964.

5. It must be noticed that in terms of the Second Proviso to Section 64 (2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
application may be entertained by the Deputy Commissioner after the expiry of period specified under Section 64 (2) (a) within a period of one year if he is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing it within the period specified in the first proviso.
6. Section 64 (2) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 reads as under:
" 64. Reference to Authority.-

3 (1) xxx NC: 2023:KHC:23788 (2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made-- (a) person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 21, or within six months from the date of the Collector's award,

whichever period shall first expire:
Provided further that the Collector may entertain an application after the expiry of the said period, within a further period of one year, if he is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing it within the period specified in the first proviso."
6. In the present case, the representation at Annexure-'B' does not have details so as to enable exercise of discretion by the Deputy Commissioner under the proviso.

In light of the same, it would meet the ends of justice to set aside the endorsement at Annexure-'D' on the ground that the authority has not taken note of the power of extension provided for in proviso to Section 64.
NC: 2023:KHC:23788 7.

The endorsement having been set aside, the matter is remitted back to the authority to reconsider the representation at Annexure-B along with further representation that may be made by the petitioner making out a case for extension in terms of second proviso to Section 2.
Such an application to be made within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order.
If grounds are made out in the application, the authority may consider the same and pass suitable orders in accordance with law.
8. Accordingly, the matter is relegated to the Assistant Commissioner, Land Acquisition, Bangalore Sub-division for reconsideration in accordance with the discussion made above.
All contentions are kept open.
